Start a Presentation in Google Slides

Create and name a presentation, find your way around the Google Slides screen, pick a theme, and add slides with the right layouts.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Create a Google Slides presentation from Google Drive and give it a clear name
  • ✓Name the parts of the Slides screen: menus, toolbar, filmstrip, slide, speaker notes, Slideshow, and Share
  • ✓Apply a theme and explain what a theme changes
  • ✓Add slides, choose a layout for each one, and type into placeholders

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

A presentation for new tenants

On the job

You are the office assistant at Parkview Property Management.

Denise Carter, the office manager, wants a short welcome presentation for new tenants at Riverside Commons. It will play on the lobby screen, Denise will present it at tenant orientation, and new tenants will get a copy by email. Everyone at Parkview uses Google Workspace, so you build it in Google Slides.

Your task: Start the presentation, give it a name people can find, choose a theme, and set up the first slides.

Google Slides is Google's presentation app, the Google Workspace counterpart to Microsoft PowerPoint. It runs in a web browser, saves every change automatically to Google Drive, and lets several people work on the same presentation at once. You can use it with a personal Google Account or a work or school account.

Key terms

Presentation
A Google Slides file. PowerPoint calls it a deck or a presentation, too.
Filmstrip
The column of slide thumbnails on the left. Select a thumbnail to work on that slide.
Theme
A matched set of colors, fonts, backgrounds, and layouts that styles every slide at once.
Layout
The arrangement of placeholders on a slide, such as Title and body or Title and two columns.
Placeholder
A box on a new slide that says Click to add title or Click to add text. Click it and type.
Speaker notes
Notes under the slide for the presenter. The audience doesn't see them.

Create and name a presentation

  1. In Google Drive, open the folder the presentation belongs in (for Parkview, Riverside Commons).
  2. Select New › Google Slides. Choose Blank presentation, or From a template to start from a design. (You can also go to slides.google.com and start a new presentation there.)
  3. The new presentation opens in a new tab, named Untitled presentation. Click that name at the top left, type a name, and press Enter.
  4. There's no Save button. Slides saves each change to Drive as you work.
💡 Name files so a coworker can find them by searching Drive: what it is, plus the building or date it's for. “New Tenant Welcome - Riverside Commons” is easy to find. “Untitled presentation” and “slides final v2” are not.

The Google Slides screen

Choose a theme

A theme styles the whole presentation at once: background, colors, fonts, and the look of every layout. Choose the theme early, before you style individual slides, so all slides match.

  • Select Slide › Change theme (or Theme on the toolbar). The Themes panel opens on the right.
  • Select a theme to apply it to every slide. Close the panel when you're done.
  • Your organization may give you a branded theme or template. In the Themes panel, Import theme brings in the theme from another presentation.
  • To change the theme's colors for the whole file, use Slide › Edit theme. Changes there apply to every slide that uses the theme.
PowerPoint users: Slides' themes work like the themes on PowerPoint's Design tab, and Slide › Edit theme is similar to PowerPoint's Slide Master view.

Add slides and pick layouts

  • To add a slide, select New slide (+) at the top left. The new slide uses the same layout as the slide you're on.
  • To add a slide with a different layout, select the arrow next to New slide and choose the layout.
  • To change the layout of an existing slide, select the slide, then select Layout on the toolbar (or Slide › Apply layout) and choose a new one. Your text moves into the new placeholders.
  • Click a placeholder (Click to add title, Click to add text) and type. Text in a body placeholder becomes a bulleted list when you press Enter.

Worked example

Setting up the welcome presentation

Create the presentation and the first two slides.

  1. 1

    In Drive, open Riverside Commons, then New › Google Slides.

    Creating it inside the building's folder means it's filed, and shared, with that building's files from the start.

  2. 2

    Rename it New Tenant Welcome - Riverside Commons.

    A clear name makes it easy to search for.

  3. 3

    Choose the Streamline theme.

    Choosing a theme first styles every slide you add afterward.

  4. 4

    Type the title on slide 1, then New slide › Title and body and type “Your First Week”.

    Each slide gets the layout that fits its content.

Result: A named, themed presentation with a title slide and a first content slide.

🔑 Folder, name, theme, then slides: in that order, the file stays organized and consistent.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Build the start of a presentation in your own Google Account (a free personal account works) or your school account.

  1. In Google Drive, create a folder named Slides Practice. In it, select New › Google Slides › Blank presentation.
  2. Name the presentation “Welcome to [your town or school]”.
  3. Apply any theme.
  4. Add three more slides: one Title and body, one Title and two columns, and one Section header. Type a title on each.
  5. Change the layout of one slide to a different layout.
Deliverable: Submit a screenshot showing the presentation's name and the filmstrip with all four slides to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Google Slides, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
